title: The Horizon of the Upper Fly River
premise: Rafael Montrose, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Voss syndicate, is forced by her old rival Dario Kell to lead a crew up Papua New Guinea's Fly River to recover a lost survey cache from her father's final expedition—the one that killed him and three others twelve years ago. The job was sworn off because the source region is taboo to the local clans who guard it as ancestral memory made landscape. As the dry season drains the river and the crew fractures under Voss pressure, Rafael discovers the 'cache' is actually her father's evidence of a land-fraud scheme implicating both Voss and the government survey office. She must choose between paying her debt with the documents or delivering them upstream to the clan elders whose justice operates entirely outside any court. In the end she burns her own escape route—literally destroying the crew's fuel barge—to carry the truth to the source, trading her freedom for her father's name and finding that memory, not money, is the only inheritance worth keeping.
about_author: Petra Okafor is a former hydrologist who spent six years documenting river communities across West Africa and Melanesia before turning to fiction. Her debut novel draws on fieldwork among communities whose legal traditions run deeper than the maps drawn over them.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Chasing a supercell across the Oklahoma panhandle, she measures her life in odometer readings while dodging calls from Voss collectors. Establishes her debt, her restlessness, and the rule she lives by: never stay anywhere long enough to be found. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as freedom.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kept Receipts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Dario Kell finds her at a roadside diner, twelve years after their falling-out, holding a contract from Voss: guide an expedition up the Fly River to a survey cache her father hid before dying. The debt vanishes if she says yes. Emotional beat: dread wearing the mask of opportunity.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. In Port Moresby, Dario assembles the team—a disgraced geologist, a mercenary named Ilsa, a young translator named Tomo—and realizes Rafael hasn't told them what the job really is. He justifies his own silence. Emotional beat: complicity.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Tomo's POV. The crew launches onto the Fly. Tomo, whose grandmother's village lies upstream, translates for the boatmen and hears them refuse to pass the gorge at Kiunga. First hint that the river itself has laws older than contracts. Emotional beat: unease.

chapters.title: Twelve Years Downstream
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Flashback woven into the present: her father's last radio call, the expedition that never returned, the inquest that blamed him. She admits to herself she took this job to find out what he actually hid. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing like a drowned log.

chapters.title: The Optimists Call
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. A satellite call from Voss's enforcer, Mr. Adeyemi, makes clear the deadline: the cache before the dry season ends, or the debt transfers to every crew member personally. Ilsa starts calculating whether Rafael is worth more alive or dead. Emotional beat: fear curdling into pragmatism.

chapters.title: Saltwater Crocodiles and Other Creditors
chapters.summary: Geologist Wren's POV. A supply run goes wrong; a boatman is injured; the crew burns two days. Wren deciphers part of her father's old survey notes and realizes the coordinates don't point to minerals—they point to land titles. Emotional beat: dawning suspicion.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Fork
chapters.summary: Tomo's POV. At the gorge, the hired boatmen walk off despite triple pay. An elder named Yawane appears, recognizes Tomo's family name, and warns: the source holds the ancestors' testimony, and those who take from it are erased from memory. Emotional beat: the pull of belonging versus obligation.

chapters.title: Upstream on Foot
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The crew abandons the boats and treks into the headwater country. Heat, leeches, dwindling water. Dario and Rafael finally argue about the past—his betrayal during the original expedition's aftermath. Emotional beat: old wounds opened on new ground.

chapters.title: A Grave Without a Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They find the wreck of the original camp and, near it, an unmarked grave that isn't her father's. Evidence suggests someone else died here—someone the official record says survived. The fraud had a witness, and the witness didn't make it home. Emotional beat: horror at how deep the lie runs.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Advance Team
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Voss's second team appears upstream ahead of them—Ilsa's old colleagues. She secretly radios their position, hedging her bets. Rafael catches the transmission's tail and says nothing, filing it away. Emotional beat: trust beginning to rot.

chapters.title: The Dry Season Bargain
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. Water sources fail; the crew votes to turn back except Rafael, Dario, Tomo, and Ilsa. Dario confesses Voss promised him the survey office directorship if the documents come back unopened. His ambition laid bare. Emotional beat: shame.

chapters.title: Yawane's Path
chapters.summary: Tomo's POV. Yawane reappears, offering passage through clan territory—not for payment, but on condition that whatever is carried from the source be spoken aloud to the elders first. Tomo accepts on the crew's behalf without asking. Emotional beat: a promise made in another language of obligation.

chapters.title: The Cache
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. They reach the cave at the source: her father's sealed case containing land-title surveys proving Voss and the survey office sold clan territories that were never ceded. Also, her father's journal—his last entry names Dario as the man who tipped off Voss about the original route. Emotional beat: betrayal upon betrayal.

chapters.title: Guns at the Source
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Adeyemi's team arrives. Ilsa switches sides openly, then wavers when Adeyemi orders the witnesses eliminated rather than paid. A standoff in the sacred valley; Tomo steps between the barrels. Emotional beat: the moment a mercenary discovers a line she can't cross.

chapters.title: What Was Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In the firefight's chaos, Dario takes a bullet shielding the case—or appearing to. Rafael realizes the only way out is the one nobody wants: give the documents to the elders, erasing their leverage over Voss forever. She chooses justice outside the law. Emotional beat: resolve.

chapters.title: The Burning Barge
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (arriving with the retreat party). Rafael torches the fuel barge and the supply cache, stranding everyone—including herself—in the highlands so no one can carry the documents downstream. Adeyemi's team is stranded too, and furious. Emotional beat: liberation through self-destruction.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Before the elders at the source, the documents are read aloud, translated by Tomo, entered into the clan's living record—songs, not filings. Her father's name is restored; the unnamed grave receives its name and mourning rites. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into ceremony.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Walking out through clan territory over weeks, escorted by Yawane's people. Dario survives but will face the elders' judgment, not a court's. Ilsa disappears into the bush owing nothing to anyone. Rafael owes nothing either—for the first time in twelve years. Emotional beat: lightness.

chapters.title: Copies
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reaching the coast, Wren reveals she photographed key pages before the burning—insurance against Voss silencing the story. The documents begin moving toward journalists and land-rights lawyers through channels Voss can't buy. Emotional beat: cautious hope.

chapters.title: Settled Accounts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Months later, Voss's operation unravels publicly; Adeyemi is arrested on unrelated charges, the syndicate bleeding out in lawsuits it can't control. Rafael testifies not for immunity but for the record. She pays back the last of her debts with expedition wages honestly earned. Emotional beat: quiet vindication.

chapters.title: The Horizon of the Upper Fly River
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, closing frame. She returns to the plains to chase storms again—but now she stays places, keeps a plant alive, answers letters from Tomo. Standing on the flat horizon, she understands her father measured rivers because they always know where they're going. Final beat: inheritance claimed—memory as the truest map home.
